title: UM-PIM: DRAM-based PIM with Uniform & Shared Memory Space
problem: Memory interleaving and virtual memory constraints limit contiguous data visibility to PIM units, forcing fine-grained PIM tasks with high offloading overhead. Existing PIM systems disable interleaving to improve efficiency, creating a new 'system memory wall' that reduces CPU bandwidth.
motivation: Practical PIM deployment requires resolving the architectural conflict between CPU memory bandwidth efficiency and PIM task granularity without sacrificing either.
method: UM-PIM introduces a dual-track memory management system where interleaved CPU pages and non-interleaved PIM pages coexist in unified memory. Independent page allocation and address translation handle each page type; DIMM-side interface hardware provides dynamic address mapping for efficient data re-layout; optimized APIs reduce PIM-to-PIM communication overhead.
key_novelty: Enabling interleaved and non-interleaved pages to coexist in a uniform shared memory space eliminates the false choice between CPU bandwidth and PIM efficiency.
contributions: Dual-track memory management with independent page allocation and address translation for CPU and PIM pages
DIMM-side interface hardware for dynamic address mapping and accelerated data re-layout
Optimized APIs for cross-PIM communication and CPU access patterns
Zero-copy PIM offloading achieving 1.96x end-to-end speedup with <0.1% CPU degradation

metrics.speedup: 1.96x end-to-end average; 4.93x CPU time reduction on partitioned workloads
metrics.other: CPU performance degradation <0.1% vs 25.8% in current PIM systems

baselines: Current PIM systems with interleaving disabled
limitations: Specific workload characteristics, power consumption, and silicon area overhead not discussed in abstract.
